entry.title: OfinTech Desk: an open-source AI workspace for finance where every number has a source
entry.summary:
Most "AI for finance" demos have the same flaw: the model writes a confident paragraph full of numbers, and nobody can tell which of them came from the ledger and which the model made up.
**[OfinTech Desk](https://github.com/OfinTech/ofinTech-Dask)** is our answer to that, and as of **v1.0.0 (27 Oct 2026)** it is fully open source under **Apache-2.0**. It's a desktop app (plus an optional self-hosted Team Server) that reads your ledger, spreadsheets, documents and inbox, does the arithmetic *in code*, fills in your own Excel and Word files with a source for every figure, and asks a human before it sends or changes anything.

entry.summary:
The game in one paragraph
Sled Volt is a three-lane sled runner down an endless snowy mountain: change lanes, jump, tuck, grind rails, fill a frost meter and double-tap for VOLT to smash through everything, while a snow beast called the Rimehorn chases you after a stumble. entry.title: Tailworm: eleven unfixed flaws in a mesh VPN, and the SSH path that carries root
entry.summary:
Tailworm: eleven unfixed flaws in a mesh VPN, and the SSH path that carries root
A mesh VPN is usually deployed so that nobody has to publish an administrative interface. Tailscale builds a tailnet out of WireGuard peer-to-peer links, and headscale reimplements the control server for teams that want to run it themselves. That design removes public load balancers and open ports, which is why so many engineering teams treat the tailnet as an internal network with a login attached. A security audit published this week argues that the login is doing more work than the operators think. Cyberdione Labs reported eleven vulnerabilities in Tailscale 1.104.2 and in the self-hosted headscale v0.29.5 control server. The researchers grouped them under the name Tailworm and released the details public…

entry.summary: Monuments of India opens on a map of the country, not a list of files. Its 101 landmarks are pins on India's outline, coloured by kind: temples and shrines, forts and palaces, tombs and memorials, and civic and engineering works. Where several places would land on the same spot, they fold into a numbered cluster, and choosing it zooms in until the pins separate. Beside the map is a list grouped by state that narrows as you type. Pick a place and the map gives way to a 3D model you can orbit, zoom and step through with the arrow keys.
